experiment_type: paired fixed-observation snapshots, not closed-loop episodes
fairness: Identical raw scan and near scan within each pair; identical angular-bin budget, height layers, candidate library and cost. Adaptive compression uses current raw scan edges; it saves representation entries, not raw acquisition work.
risk_model: Unknown/free frontiers, per-cell observation age, 4-neighbor Dijkstra through unknown cells and around observed walls. No ground-truth walls in planning. No probabilities, ADMM, recursive feasibility, or continuous-space guarantee. Center reachability respects walls; Euclidean collision-volume inflation can conservatively mark cells on the far side of thin walls.

planning_baselines.visible_only: Same candidate library and measured-free geometry; no future hidden-agent risk.
planning_baselines.single_worst: Same library, one maximum-speed reachable-risk configuration.
planning_baselines.shared_prefix: Three speed configurations, equal-weight sum of best suffix costs, a 0.4 s common control prefix, and checked braking tails. Only the first target control may execute.

nested_branch_interpretation: The three speed-bound risk sets are nested. With the same finite candidate library, every feasible worst-case suffix can serve all branches, so shared-prefix feasibility must equal single-worst feasibility. This experiment tests consensus consistency and cost selection, not a larger safety-feasible set.
sampling_interpretation: The 32 rows are parameter combinations over 4 geometric scenes, not independent scenarios or success-rate trials. Age changes planning/freshness but repeats the same compression evidence.

published_formula_reference.scope: Equations 7/8 only, canonical visible disk fixture; not a full CMPC performance baseline.
published_formula_reference.caution: The published speed denominator becomes very conservative near zero speed; no silent denominator modification was made.

limitations: No G1/MuJoCo/CAT policy integration, learned locomotion, or closed-loop collision/success statistics.

The near grid uses 0.25 m voxels: fine only relative to far angular compression. It supports no centimeter-level foot placement or body-clearance claims; a finer grid and full body collision envelope are required before integration.
Navigation uses an upright column body and excludes the lowest ground layer. It does not model feet, articulated legs, stepping or crouching.
Zero-width rays certify uniform finite voxels only, never angular sectors or unsampled height gaps.
Near geometry is an ideal dense center-targeted 3-D scanner; its ray count grows with radius and its runtime is included.
Unknown is not safe ego space; conservative beam/height gaps can make every candidate infeasible.
All hypothetical agents follow the declared 4-neighbor grid. Continuous diagonal motion can be faster and is outside this guarantee.
No source beyond the finite map boundary; world extent is an explicit closed test domain.
All surfaces in the mapping fixture are static. Stale occupied cells stay blocked; stale free cells become unknown.
Branch score weights are heuristics, not probabilities. A feasible finite horizon does not establish recursive safety.
Display reconstruction error is a compression diagnostic; the planner uses retained rays, never fills a bin's whole wedge.
